newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close lower across the board.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close lower across the board.

text.p: Sweden's stockmarket closed lower across the board on Wednesday with losses exacerbated by a weak opening on Wall Street in afternoon trade.
The Stockholm general index fell 1.10 percent to 2141.47 after shares worth 3.4 billion crowns were traded.
Brokers said the lower U.S. opening, increasing interest rates and a weaker dollar fuelled uncertainty in the market which was riding on record highs on Monday.
The main focus of the day was Swedish vehicle maker Volvo which posted a slightly disappointing report for the first nine months of 1996. Volvo closed three crowns lower at 138.
The company's truck division was seen as most alarming.
"The result was weaker than expected even though we already knew that Trucks would have to take heavy costs in the third quarter," said Bertil Nilsson of Sweden's Nordiska brokers.
Bluechips were weaker. Telecoms giant Ericsson fell 2.5 to 180.5 crowns and drugs major Astra slipped 0.5 to 306 crowns.
The bank sector was the worst performer over the day, with the index slipping 1.83 percent. S-E-Banken was one lower at 57 crowns and Handelsbanken slipped one to 159.5 crowns.
